eDNA-first site-visit CPUE model

Corrected linkage, hierarchical BRMS, boosted trees and ensemble

Corrected observation unit

The previous operational models started from each cull dive and looked backwards for an eligible eDNA event. The corrected analysis starts with an eDNA sampling campaign and takes the first subsequent visit to every cull site. All dives at that site and date are combined into one count and effort total.

Individual eDNA-event reversal would duplicate outcomes. The selected campaign-to-site design retains 519 unique response visits with no duplication.

Hierarchical model

COTS count ~ % positive + distance + elapsed time
             + offset(log(total bottom time))
             + (1 | reef) + (1 | cull site) + (1 | eDNA campaign)

The fast GLMM screen strongly supports retaining all three grouping terms.

The production BRMS model retained 8,000 post-warmup draws. All R-hat values are 1.00 and it has no divergent transitions. Its 0.04 marginal crossing is 73.2% positive.

Boosted trees

The concentration-free Poisson boosted tree was tuned with complete eDNA campaigns held out. Its partial-dependence intervals use 100 whole-reef bootstrap samples.

Ensemble validation

All model comparisons use the same five complete-campaign holdouts.

Deployment

The versioned object is analysis/site/output/reefDNA_site_visit_model_bundle.rds. It accepts percent positive, distance, elapsed days, optional effort, reef, cull-site and campaign identifiers through reefDNA::predict_reef_cpue().

The primary outputs are calibrated exceedance probabilities and expected CPUE with uncertainty. Alert cutoffs maximize F1 on these out-of-fold predictions and should remain provisional until the operational costs of false negatives and false positives are specified.
